Two letters mirror East and West,
This points to “JFK.”
The mirrored letters are the two K’s in the broader Kennedy family political legacy — but more directly, it evokes the symmetry of the initials in the iconic abbreviation JFK (three letters forming a balanced monogram).
It can also subtly hint at the way “J” and “K” frame the name visually in the abbreviation — creating a compact, emblematic identity recognized globally across East and West.
A family name outlives the rest.
Unlike many politicians remembered individually, the Kennedy surname became a political dynasty — extending beyond John F. Kennedy to Robert Kennedy and Ted Kennedy. The “family name” became larger than the individual office-holder.
